Hi Lauren — thanks for the note and the heads-up on procurement timing. Short answers up front:

• No, Redwood does not use customer-provided inputs (requests, files, transcripts) to train or fine-tune any models that serve other customers.
• We retain operational telemetry for short windows to support reliability and billing, and we have documented deletion pathways for customer-requested erasure.

I'm looping Neha from Security & Compliance for the formal wording and the certificate, and Grace from Ops for the retention/playbook details. I've attached a one-page Model Exclusion statement for immediate use and our deletion playbook for your legal team.

Hi Lauren — context and formal language below you can copy into the SOW; happy to generate a signed PDF.

Formal statement (summary):
Redwood Inference does not use customer-supplied content (including API requests, uploaded files, transcripts, or metadata) to train or refine models used to serve other customers. Customer data is isolated per account and is not part of any training corpus.

Retention and deletion details (nuances):
• Primary store: Customer data persisted in their tenant is retained according to the agreed TTL; typical default is 30 days for request payloads unless otherwise configured in the account.
• Short-term telemetry: Aggregated service telemetry (metrics, error traces) may be retained up to 90 days for debugging and reliability improvements; this telemetry is pseudonymized and not attached to account identifiers used for model training.
• Backups & snapshots: Periodic backups and snapshots are retained for disaster recovery. When an erase request is issued, we initiate a tombstone process and schedule deletion from backups according to our backup retention windows; we provide a signed certificate once the process completes.
• Erase window & verification: Standard erase completion target is 30 days for primary stores; backup purging may take up to an additional 60 days depending on snapshot schedules. We provide a verification artifact (audit log entries + deletion job ids) and can produce an attestation for procurement.
• Region considerations: For customers on Dedicated/Private deployments or in EU regions, we ensure data residency and deletion follow region-specific controls and can provide region-specific evidence.

Limitations and operational impact:
• A request-scoped cache (short-lived KV) may persist transiently to meet latency SLOs but is cleared as part of the erase workflow.
• Deleting data mid-rollout of model changes may impact the ability to retroactively debug a specific request; we coordinate with customers on trade-offs for compliance-first deletes.

If you want a concise single-paragraph attestation for the SOW I can provide it and stamp it with our security team. If you need DocuSign, please send the DocuSign envelope or we can initiate one.
